content.text:
Preserve:

- [#136](https://github.com/johnnylarner/exposed/pull/136) deliberately matches the **entire exact parsed name**, gated to explicit individual/person donors. Keep raw spelling, scorer names, extracted evidence, and role/type boundaries.
- [#23](https://github.com/johnnylarner/exposed/pull/23) explicitly acknowledges same-name false positives. [#27](https://github.com/johnnylarner/exposed/pull/27) keeps insufficiently supported similarities reviewable and prevents unrelated organisations merging.

Change:

- The observed peerage variant exceeds #136’s supported examples: its regression covers `Lord David Sainsbury`, `David Sainsbury`, and `Lord (David) Sainsbury`; it does not establish title-only peerage names as equivalent.
- A reviewed grouping mechanism already exists in `exposed/src/lib/domain/models/funder_grouping.rs:36`. Its finite typed enum currently contains BBC, GB News, and Premier League. Definitions provide explicit source names and a preferred label.

Avoid:

- Do not infer identity from surname equality or remove name tokens globally.
- Do not confuse post-load reviewed groups with resolver identities. [#52](https://github.com/johnnylarner/exposed/pull/52) introduced groups to combine browsing/search results while retaining source IDs and direct evidence.
- Reviewed-family eligibility currently checks canonical stored names, **not aliases** (`funder_grouping.rs:224`); a test explicitly protects that distinction.

Risk:

- [#57](https://github.com/johnnylarner/exposed/pull/57) rejects components containing conflicting reviewed families. Preferred labels are independent of representative UUIDs; alias-only groups retain their fallback.
- Reviewed-policy changes require rebuilding and refreshing the projection. [#66](https://github.com/johnnylarner/exposed/pull/66) removed the standalone refresh command: refresh now occurs through declaration loading, including an exact unchanged-artifact retry.
- Source history establishes conservative mechanism boundaries, but supplies no reviewed evidence that the three specific Sainsbury strings denote the same person. That identity assertion needs evidence beyond the parser/history.

Consulted local git history/blame and PRs #23, #27, #52, #57, #66, #136 only; no files changed.
